articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Non-authoritative conceptual foundation guiding the FASB in developing US GAAP, covering the objective of financial reporting (Ch. 1), reporting entity (Ch. 2), qualitative characteristics (Ch. 3), elements (Ch. 4), recognition and derecognition (Ch. 5), measurement (Ch. 6, issued 2024), presentation (Ch. 7), and notes to financial statements (Ch. 8).

articles.heading: Conceptual Foundation & 2024 Measurement Chapter
articles.text:
• Fundamental Qualitative Characteristics (Ch. 3): Relevance (predictive/confirmatory value, materiality) and Faithful Representation (complete, neutral, free from error).
• Elements of Financial Statements (Ch. 4): Asset = present right of an entity to an economic benefit; Liability = present obligation to transfer an economic benefit.
• Measurement (Ch. 6, issued June 2024): Establishes entry price system vs. exit price system as the two overarching measurement frameworks.
• Non-authoritative status: Concepts Statements do not override authoritative ASC guidance (ASC 105-10-05-3).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Largely converged with the IASB Conceptual Framework (2018), though FASB retains its own chapters on Measurement (2024) and Notes (Ch. 8) and places Concepts Statements strictly outside the authoritative GAAP hierarchy.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes the FASB Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) as the single source of authoritative nongovernmental US GAAP (alongside SEC rules/interpretive releases for SEC registrants).

articles.heading: Single-Level GAAP Hierarchy & Non-Authoritative Guidance
articles.text:
• Authoritative Sources (ASC 105-10-05-1): Only two levels exist — authoritative (the ASC + SEC guidance for registrants) and non-authoritative.
• Analogizing (ASC 105-10-05-2): If a transaction is not specified in the ASC, first analogize to similar transactions within the ASC before consulting non-authoritative sources (CON 8, AICPA guides, IFRS).
• True-and-Fair Override: Unlike IAS 1.19, US GAAP effectively prohibits departing from authoritative GAAP in SEC filings.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • IFRS (IAS 8.10–12) provides a formal hierarchy allowing management to look to other standard-setters (including US GAAP) when no IFRS applies; US GAAP centers strictly on the Codification.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Provides baseline presentation rules for financial statements, including Discontinued Operations (ASC 205-20), Liquidation Basis of Accounting (ASC 205-30), and Going Concern disclosures (ASC 205-40).

articles.heading: Discontinued Operations, Liquidation Basis & Going Concern
articles.text:
• Discontinued Operations (ASC 205-20): Requires disposal of a component/group of components to represent a 'strategic shift' having a major effect on operations and financial results.
• Liquidation Basis (ASC 205-30): Mandatory when liquidation is 'imminent', measuring assets at expected cash collection amounts and accruing liquidation costs.
• Going Concern (ASC 205-40): Management must evaluate whether substantial doubt exists within ONE YEAR after the date the financial statements are issued (or available to be issued).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text:
• Going Concern look-forward window: ASC 205-40 measures 12 months from the financial statement ISSUANCE date, whereas IAS 1.26 measures at least 12 months from the REPORTING (balance sheet) date.
• Discontinued Operations: ASC 205-20 requires a 'strategic shift', a narrower bar than IFRS 5.32 ('separate major line of business or geographical area').

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Addresses general balance sheet classification (current vs. noncurrent assets/liabilities, working capital) and strict right-of-setoff / master netting arrangement rules (ASC 210-20).

articles.heading: Current/Noncurrent Classification & Right of Setoff
articles.text:
• General Offsetting (ASC 210-20-45-1): Permitted only when four conditions are met (determinable amounts, right to set off, intent to set off, enforceable at law).
• Derivative / Repo Exception (ASC 210-20-45-11): Permits net presentation of derivatives and cash collateral executed under an enforceable master netting arrangement even WITHOUT intent to settle net.
• Debt Classification: Refinancing completed AFTER the balance sheet date but BEFORE issuance can support noncurrent classification under ASC 470-10 (contrast with IAS 1).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Offsetting Derivatives: US GAAP allows net balance sheet presentation under master netting agreements (ASC 210-20), whereas IAS 32.42 strictly requires BOTH a legally enforceable right AND intent to settle net/simultaneously — making US bank balance sheets appear smaller than IFRS peers.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Governs presentation of net income, Other Comprehensive Income (OCI), Accumulated OCI (AOCI), and footnote disaggregation of income statement expenses (ASC 220-40, added by ASU 2024-03).

articles.heading: OCI Presentation & ASU 2024-03 Expense Disaggregation (DISE)
articles.text:
• Single or Two-Statement Approach (ASC 220-10-45): Present comprehensive income in one continuous statement or two consecutive statements.
• Recycling: Virtually all US GAAP OCI items (AFS debt unrealized gains/losses, cash flow hedges, pension adjustments, CTA) recycle to net income (unlike IFRS equity FVOCI).
• Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses — DISE (ASC 220-40, ASU 2024-03, effective fiscal years beginning after Dec 15, 2026): Public business entities must disclose tabular breakdowns in footnotes for purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, intangible amortization, and DD&A embedded in each income statement expense line.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Structure vs. IFRS 18: IFRS 18 mandates three standardized face-of-P&L categories (Operating, Investing, Financing) plus MPM disclosures; US GAAP (ASU 2024-03) leaves the face of the income statement flexible (SEC Reg S-X drives public company lines) and requires granular expense disaggregation in the footnotes.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes classification of cash receipts and payments into Operating, Investing, and Financing activities, including strict rules for restricted cash (ASC 230-10-45-4) and interest/dividends.

articles.heading: Cash Flow Classification & Restricted Cash Rules
articles.text:
• Strict Classification (ASC 230-10-45): Interest paid, interest received, and dividends received are ALWAYS Operating; dividends paid are ALWAYS Financing.
• Restricted Cash (ASU 2016-18): Beginning and ending cash totals on the Statement of Cash Flows MUST include restricted cash and restricted cash equivalents, with a reconciliation to the balance sheet.
• Bank Overdrafts: Classified as Financing activities (not negative cash equivalents).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text:
• Interest & Dividends: US GAAP fixes interest paid/received and dividends received in Operating; IFRS 18 (effective 2027) classifies interest/dividends paid in Financing and interest/dividends received in Investing (for non-financial entities).
• Bank Overdrafts: IAS 7.8 allows repayable-on-demand overdrafts to be included in cash & cash equivalents; ASC 230 treats them as Financing.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Addresses retrospective application of accounting principle changes, prospective accounting for estimate changes, reporting entity changes, and restatement of prior-period financial statements for errors.

articles.heading: Preferability, Estimates, Big R vs. Little r Restatements
articles.text:
• Voluntary Accounting Principle Change (ASC 250-10-45-2): Allowed only if management justifies the new principle as 'preferable' (SEC registrants require a preferability letter from the independent auditor); applied retrospectively.
• Change in Accounting Estimate (ASC 250-10-45-17): Applied prospectively; changes in depreciation/amortization method are accounted for as a change in estimate effected by a change in principle.
• Error Corrections (ASC 250-10-45-22): Material prior-period errors require 'Big R' restatement (reissuance); immaterial prior errors that would be material if corrected in the current period require 'little r' revision of comparatives (SAB 108 dual rollover/iron-curtain assessment).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Substantially converged with IAS 8, except US GAAP requires an explicit auditor preferability letter for SEC registrants making voluntary policy changes and has formalized 'Big R' vs. 'little r' SEC restatement practice.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes computation and presentation of Basic and Diluted EPS for public entities, including the two-class method for participating securities, treasury stock method, and if-converted method.

articles.heading: Basic/Diluted EPS, Two-Class & If-Converted Methods
articles.text:
• Treasury Stock Method (ASC 260-10-45-23): Applied to options and warrants; assumed proceeds include unrecognized compensation cost for share-based awards.
• Convertible Instruments (ASU 2020-06): Eliminates the treasury stock method for convertible debt settled in cash/shares, requiring the 'if-converted' method (with interest add-back and full share dilution unless principal must be settled in cash).
• Two-Class Method (ASC 260-10-45-60): Mandatory when participating securities (e.g., unvested RSAs with nonforfeitable dividends) exist.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Year-to-date Diluted EPS: ASC 260 averages incremental shares from each interim period, whereas IAS 33 computes YTD diluted EPS independently on a cumulative YTD basis (can yield different results when stock prices fluctuate).

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Prescribes accounting and disclosure principles for interim periods (quarterly 10-Q reporting), adopting an 'integral' view where each interim period is viewed primarily as an integral part of the annual period.

articles.heading: Integral Approach to Interim Periods
articles.text:
• Integral View (ASC 270-10-45-1): Certain annual costs (e.g., property taxes, annual bonuses, volume rebates, LIFO liquidations expected to be replaced by year-end) are allocated/deferred across interim periods.
• Income Taxes (ASC 740-270): Computed using the estimated Annual Effective Tax Rate (AETR) applied to YTD ordinary income, with discrete items recognized in the quarter incurred.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Integral vs. Discrete View: ASC 270 follows an INTEGRAL approach (allowing deferral of certain interim variances/costs expected to reverse by year-end), whereas IAS 34 follows a DISCRETE approach (each interim period stands alone, except for annual effective tax rate).

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Requires public entities to report operating segment information through the eyes of the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM), significantly expanded by ASU 2023-07 to mandate disclosure of significant segment expenses.

articles.heading: CODM Approach & ASU 2023-07 Significant Segment Expenses
articles.text:
• Identification & Aggregation (ASC 280-10-50-1 to 50-12): Operating segments identified via CODM review; quantitative 10% revenue/profit/asset thresholds and 75% consolidated external revenue coverage test.
• Significant Segment Expenses (ASU 2023-07, effective FY2024+): Must disclose significant segment expense categories regularly provided to the CODM and included in segment profit/loss, plus the title/position of the CODM and single-reportable-segment entity disclosures.
• Multiple Profit Measures: ASU 2023-07 permits disclosing additional CODM profit measures alongside the measure most consistent with GAAP.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Converged with IFRS 8 on the CODM management approach, though ASU 2023-07's mandatory significant segment expense table goes beyond current IFRS 8 requirements; matrix organizations use products/services under ASC 280-10-50-9.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes the three-category classification model for debt securities — Held-to-Maturity (HTM), Trading, and Available-for-Sale (AFS) — and their balance sheet/OCI accounting.

articles.heading: HTM, Trading & Available-for-Sale (AFS) Debt Classification
articles.text:
• Held-to-Maturity — HTM (ASC 320-10-25-1): Amortized cost; requires positive intent and ability to hold to maturity (selling HTM triggers strict 'tainting' rules).
• Trading: Measured at fair value through net income (FVTPL).
• Available-for-Sale — AFS: Measured at fair value with unrealized gains/losses in OCI (recycled to net income upon sale); credit losses recorded via allowance under ASC 326-30 (capped at fair value floor).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Classification Driver: US GAAP classifies debt securities by management intent (HTM/Trading/AFS) without an SPPI cash-flow test; IFRS 9 classifies financial assets by BOTH Business Model AND SPPI contractual cash flow characteristics.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Requires all equity investments without significant influence or control to be measured at Fair Value Through Net Income (FVTPL), with an optional measurement alternative for equity securities without a readily determinable fair value.

articles.heading: Mandatory FVTPL & Measurement Alternative for Private Equity
articles.text:
• Default Rule (ASC 321-10-35-1): All equity securities (outside equity method/consolidation) are measured at fair value with changes recognized in NET INCOME — NO FVOCI election exists under US GAAP.
• Measurement Alternative (ASC 321-10-35-2): For equity securities without a readily determinable fair value, entities may elect cost minus impairment, plus or minus observable price changes in orderly transactions for identical/similar investments of the same issuer.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 9 / CAS 22: IFRS 9.5.7.5 allows an irrevocable FVOCI election for strategic non-trading equity investments (never recycled to P&L); US GAAP (ASC 321) PROHIBITS FVOCI for equity securities — all fair value swings hit Net Income.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Governs accounting for investments where the investor exercises significant influence (presumed at 20%–50% voting stock, or >3%–5% for limited partnerships/LLCs) and corporate joint ventures.

articles.heading: Significant Influence, Equity Method & Impairment
articles.text:
• Significant Influence Thresholds (ASC 323-10-15): Generally 20%–50% voting stock for corporations; much lower threshold (>3%–5%) for limited partnerships/LLCs maintaining specific ownership accounts.
• Fair Value Option (ASC 825-10): Any investor may elect FVTPL for an equity method investment at inception (unlike IAS 28, which restricts FVTPL to venture capital/mutual funds).
• Impairment (ASC 323-10-35-32): Written down to fair value only when a decline in value is 'other than temporary' (OTTI); impairment reversals are PROHIBITED.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text:
• Uniform Accounting Policies: IAS 28.35 requires aligning the investee's accounting policies to the investor's; ASC 323 does NOT require conforming accounting policies if the investee follows a valid GAAP alternative.
• Impairment Reversal: Prohibited under ASC 323; permitted under IAS 36.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Replaces the incurred loss model with the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) model, requiring immediate Day-1 recognition of full lifetime expected credit losses for financial assets measured at amortized cost.

articles.heading: Day-1 Lifetime CECL vs. AFS Debt Credit Loss Model
articles.text:
• Amortized Cost Assets (ASC 326-20): Measure lifetime expected credit losses upon origination/acquisition using historical loss experience, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts (reverting to historical loss thereafter).
• Pooled Assessment: Assets sharing similar risk characteristics MUST be evaluated collectively on a pool basis.
• AFS Debt Securities (ASC 326-30): Do NOT use CECL; evaluated individually when FV < amortized cost, with credit loss allowance capped at the excess of amortized cost over fair value (fair value floor).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 9 / CAS 22: ASC 326 recognizes FULL LIFETIME expected credit losses on Day 1 for all amortized-cost loans (creating larger Day-1 provisions); IFRS 9 uses a 3-stage model recognizing only 12-month ECL on Day 1 (Stage 1) and moving to lifetime ECL only after a Significant Increase in Credit Risk (Stage 2).

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes cost determination (FIFO, Weighted Average, Specific Identification, and LIFO) and subsequent measurement of inventory at Lower of Cost and Net Realizable Value (LCNRV) or Lower of Cost or Market (LCM for LIFO/retail).

articles.heading: LIFO Costing, LCNRV vs. LCM & Prohibition of Reversals
articles.text:
• Cost Formulas (ASC 330-10-30-9): FIFO, Average Cost, Specific Identification, AND Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) are all permitted (subject to IRS LIFO conformity rule if used for US tax).
• Subsequent Measurement (ASC 330-10-35): FIFO & Average Cost inventory is measured at Lower of Cost and NRV (LCNRV); LIFO and Retail Inventory Method remain measured at Lower of Cost or Market (replacement cost bounded by NRV ceiling and NRV-less-normal-profit floor).
• Write-Down Reversals (ASC 330-10-35-14): Once inventory is written down below cost, the reduced amount establishes a NEW cost basis — reversals in subsequent periods are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Two Iconic US GAAP vs. IFRS/CAS Divergences: (1) LIFO is PERMITTED under ASC 330 but PROHIBITED under IAS 2.25 and CAS 1; (2) Reversal of prior inventory write-downs is PROHIBITED under ASC 330 but REQUIRED (up to original cost) under IAS 2.33 and CAS 1.

articles.text: Governs goodwill impairment testing at the Reporting Unit level (single-step FV < carrying amount), indefinite/finite-lived intangibles, internal-use software (ASC 350-40), and fair value accounting for crypto assets (ASC 350-60, ASU 2023-08).

articles.heading: Goodwill Reporting Units, Cloud Computing & Crypto Assets
articles.text:
• Goodwill Impairment (ASC 350-20-35): Tested annually (or upon triggering event) at the Reporting Unit level (operating segment or one level below). Optional qualitative 'Step 0' screen; quantitative test compares Reporting Unit fair value to carrying amount (no reversal allowed).
• Internal-Use Software & Cloud Computing (ASC 350-40): Capitalize application-development-stage costs and qualifying cloud implementation costs; expense preliminary and post-implementation costs.
• Crypto Assets (ASC 350-60, ASU 2023-08, effective FY2025+): In-scope fungible crypto assets (e.g., Bitcoin, Ether) MUST be measured at fair value each period with changes in NET INCOME, presented separately on the balance sheet and income statement.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text:
• Goodwill Testing Level & Model: US GAAP tests at the Reporting Unit level using Fair Value only; IAS 36 tests at the CGU level using Recoverable Amount (higher of FVLCD and VIU).
• Crypto Assets: ASC 350-60 mandates FVTPL for qualifying crypto assets; under IFRS (IFRIC Agenda Decision 2019), crypto is typically an indefinite-lived intangible under IAS 38 (cost model or revaluation through OCI).

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Covers historical-cost accounting for PP&E, depreciation, the two-step undiscounted-cash-flow impairment test for long-lived assets held and used (ASC 360-10-35), and held-for-sale classification.

articles.heading: Historical Cost Only, 2-Step Impairment Test & No Reversals
articles.text:
• No Revaluation Model: PP&E MUST be carried at historical cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment — upward revaluation is strictly prohibited.
• 2-Step Impairment Test (ASC 360-10-35-17): Step 1 (Recoverability) compares carrying amount of the asset group to UNDISCOUNTED future cash flows; only if Step 1 fails does Step 2 measure impairment as carrying amount minus Fair Value.
• Impairment Reversal: Prohibited for held-and-used assets (ASC 360-10-35-20); permitted up to prior carrying amount only for assets classified as Held for Sale.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Two Major Divergences from IAS 16 / IAS 36: (1) ASC 360 uses a 2-step UNDISCOUNTED recoverability screen (fewer impairments triggered than IAS 36's 1-step discounted recoverable amount); (2) Impairment reversals and upward revaluation are prohibited under US GAAP (both permitted under IFRS).

articles.text: Requires recognition of legal obligations associated with the retirement of tangible long-lived assets (ARO, ASC 410-20) at fair value (discounted at credit-adjusted risk-free rate) and environmental remediation liabilities (ASC 410-30).

articles.heading: ARO Credit-Adjusted Discount Rate & Layer Accounting
articles.text:
• Scope (ASC 410-20): Applies to LEGAL obligations (statute, contract, promissory estoppel) — excludes purely constructive obligations.
• Discount Rate: Credit-adjusted risk-free rate locked in per cash-flow layer (upward revisions create a new layer at current rate; downward revisions use historical rate).
• Environmental Obligations (ASC 410-30): Recognized when probable and reasonably estimable (generally undiscounted unless timing/amount are fixed or reliably determinable).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IAS 37 / IFRIC 1: IAS 37 includes CONSTRUCTIVE obligations and remeasures the entire provision each period using the current pre-tax market discount rate; ASC 410-20 covers legal obligations only and locks historical credit-adjusted rates by layer.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes recognition and disclosure rules for loss contingencies (ASC 450-20) and gain contingencies (ASC 450-30), using the higher US GAAP 'probable' threshold (~70%–75%+).

articles.heading: Probable Threshold (~75%), Range Minimum & Gain Contingencies
articles.text:
• Loss Contingency Recognition (ASC 450-20-25-2): Accrue when (a) probable (likely to occur, ~70%–75%+ in US practice) AND (b) reasonably estimable.
• Range of Loss (ASC 450-20-30-1): If no point within a range is a better estimate than any other, accrue the MINIMUM amount in the range and disclose the upper bound.
• Discounting: Generally prohibited unless amount and timing of cash payments are fixed or reliably determinable.
• Gain Contingencies (ASC 450-30): Never recognized prior to realization.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Two Classic Divergences from IAS 37 / CAS 13: (1) Recognition threshold — ASC 450 'probable' (~70–75%+) is significantly higher than IAS 37 'more likely than not' (>50%); (2) Equal-probability range — ASC 450 accrues the MINIMUM of the range, whereas IAS 37 accrues the MIDPOINT (expected value for large populations).

articles.text: Governs classification of debt (callable/refinanced obligations), simplified convertible debt accounting without cash-conversion/CCF bifurcation (ASC 470-20, ASU 2020-06), and debt modifications/extinguishments (ASC 470-50, 10% cash-flow test).

articles.heading: Convertible Debt (ASU 2020-06) & 10% Modification Test
articles.text:
• Convertible Debt (ASC 470-20, ASU 2020-06): Eliminated beneficial conversion feature (BCF) and cash conversion separation models — most convertible debt is now accounted for as a SINGLE liability at amortized cost (unless embedded derivative bifurcation applies under ASC 815).
• Debt Modifications (ASC 470-50-40-10): Substantially different terms (>= 10% change in PV of cash flows) trigger extinguishment accounting (gain/loss in P&L); < 10% is accounted for prospectively via a new effective interest rate (no immediate P&L gain/loss!).
• Debt Issuance Costs (ASC 835-30): Presented as a direct deduction from the carrying amount of the debt liability.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text:
• Convertible Debt: IAS 32 ALWAYS requires split accounting (liability + equity component) for compound convertible bonds; ASU 2020-06 accounts for most US GAAP convertible bonds as a single liability.
• Non-Substantial Modification (<10%): IFRS 9.5.4.3 requires an IMMEDIATE P&L gain/loss (recalculating PV at original EIR); ASC 470-50 amortizes the difference prospectively with NO Day-1 P&L gain/loss.

articles.heading: Liability Classification, Indexation (ASC 815-40) & Mezzanine Equity
articles.text:
• Three Mandatory Liability Classes (ASC 480-10-25): (1) Mandatorily redeemable financial instruments; (2) Obligations to repurchase issuer's equity shares by transferring assets; (3) Certain obligations to issue a variable number of shares based predominantly on a fixed monetary amount.
• Temporary / Mezzanine Equity (ASC 480-10-S99-3A): SEC registrants must present conditionally redeemable preferred stock (e.g., VC preferred with change-of-control redemption) outside permanent equity in 'mezzanine' equity.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IAS 32 / CAS 37: Under IAS 32, conditionally redeemable preferred shares (outside the issuer's sole control) are generally FINANCIAL LIABILITIES; under US GAAP (ASC 480 + SEC S99-3A), they are classified in Temporary/Mezzanine Equity (between liabilities and stockholders' equity), avoiding P&L fair-value swings.

articles.heading: Five-Step Model, Licensing IP & Key US GAAP Elections
articles.text:
• Five-Step Core Principle (ASC 606-10-05-4): (1) Identify contract (collectibility = 'probable', ~75%+); (2) Identify distinct performance obligations (shipping/handling may be elected as a fulfillment activity); (3) Determine transaction price (variable consideration constraint, significant financing component, non-cash consideration measured at contract inception); (4) Allocate transaction price via SSP; (5) Recognize revenue over time or at a point in time.
• Licensing Intellectual Property (ASC 606-10-55-58): Distinguishes 'Functional IP' (point in time, e.g., software, films) vs. 'Symbolic IP' (over time, e.g., brands, logos).
• Sales Tax Election (ASC 606-10-32-2A): Policy election to exclude all sales/similar taxes from the transaction price.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Subtle Divergences from IFRS 15 / CAS 14: (1) Step 1 Collectibility — ASC 606 'probable' (~75%+) is higher than IFRS 15 (>50%); (2) Shipping & Handling — ASC 606 permits an explicit fulfillment-cost election after control transfer (not in IFRS 15); (3) Non-cash consideration — ASC 606 mandates measurement at contract inception (IFRS 15 does not specify date); (4) IP licensing uses Functional vs. Symbolic distinction.

articles.heading: Corridor Amortization, Expected Return & Prior Service Cost
articles.text:
• Net Periodic Benefit Cost: Service cost is presented with other compensation costs; non-service components (interest cost, expected return on plan assets, amortizations) are presented outside operating income (ASU 2017-07).
• Actuarial Gains/Losses & Prior Service Cost: Initially recorded in OCI and subsequently AMORTIZED (recycled) into net income (corridor approach or systematic method).
• Expected Return on Plan Assets: Uses expected long-term rate of return on plan assets (not the discount rate).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IAS 19 / CAS 9: IAS 19 calculates a single 'net interest' using the discount rate, recognizes past service cost IMMEDIATELY in P&L, and NEVER recycles OCI remeasurements to P&L; ASC 715 uses expected return on plan assets and recycles actuarial gains/losses and prior service cost from AOCI into P&L.

articles.heading: Grant-Date Fair Value, Graded Vesting & Forfeiture Policy
articles.text:
• Service/Performance/Market Conditions (ASC 718-10-30): Service & performance conditions affect quantity of awards vested; market conditions (e.g., TSR) are baked into grant-date fair value.

articles.heading: Enacted Tax Rates, Valuation Allowance, UTPs & ASU 2023-09
articles.text:
• Enacted Rates Only (ASC 740-10-30-8): Deferred taxes MUST use ENACTED tax rates (not 'substantively enacted').
• Valuation Allowance (ASC 740-10-30-5): Recognize all DTAs in full, then reduce via a contra-asset Valuation Allowance if it is 'more likely than not' (>50%) that some portion will not be realized.
• Uncertain Tax Positions — UTPs (ASC 740-10-25-6): 2-step model — Step 1: Recognition requires >50% ('more likely than not') technical merits; Step 2: Measurement at the largest amount with >50% cumulative likelihood of realization.
• ASU 2023-09 (effective FY2025+ for PBEs): Mandates standardized 8-category tabular rate reconciliation (both % and dollar amounts) and disaggregated income taxes paid by federal/state/foreign jurisdiction (>=5% threshold).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Key Divergences from IAS 12 / CAS 18: (1) Enacted vs. substantively enacted rates; (2) Intra-entity inventory transfers — ASC 740 defers seller's tax expense as a prepaid until sold to third party (IAS 12 recognizes DTA immediately at buyer's rate); (3) UTPs — ASC 740 uses cumulative-probability largest >50% amount (IFRIC 23 uses most likely amount or expected value); (4) Pillar Two — FASB treats GloBE as an Alternative Minimum Tax (period cost, no deferred tax).

articles.heading: Screen Test, Full Goodwill, Pushdown Accounting & JV Formation
articles.text:
• Definition of a Business — Screen Test (ASC 805-10-55-5A): If substantially all fair value of gross assets acquired is concentrated in a single identifiable asset (or group of similar assets), it is an ASSET acquisition, NOT a business combination.
• Noncontrolling Interest (NCI): MUST be measured at FAIR VALUE (full goodwill method only — no proportionate-share partial goodwill option).
• Pushdown Accounting (ASC 805-50-25-4): An acquired entity may ELECT to apply pushdown accounting in its standalone financial statements upon a change-in-control event.
• Joint Venture Formations (ASU 2023-05, effective Jan 1, 2025): Newly formed JVs measure contributed net assets at fair value upon formation.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Key Divergences from IFRS 3 / CAS 20: (1) NCI measurement — ASC 805 requires FAIR VALUE (full goodwill), whereas IFRS 3 allows an election between fair value and proportionate share of identifiable net assets; (2) Pushdown accounting — permitted under ASC 805-50, not permitted under IFRS; (3) Contingent liabilities — ASC 805 recognizes at FV only if determinable during measurement period (otherwise falls back to ASC 450).

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes the two-tier US GAAP consolidation framework: first evaluate the Variable Interest Entity (VIE) model (primary beneficiary = power + economics), then the Voting Interest Entity (VOE) model (>50% voting shares).

articles.heading: Dual Consolidation Model: VIE Primary Beneficiary & VOE
articles.text:
• Step 1 — VIE Model (ASC 810-10-15 / 25): An entity is a VIE if equity at risk is insufficient, equity holders lack decision-making power/obligation to absorb losses/right to receive residual returns, or voting rights are disproportionate. The Primary Beneficiary consolidates when it has BOTH (a) power to direct activities that most significantly impact economic performance AND (b) obligation to absorb losses or right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant.
• Step 2 — Voting Interest Model: If not a VIE, consolidation generally requires >50% of voting shares (no 'de facto' control concept).
• Deconsolidation (ASC 810-10-40): Full gain/loss in P&L with retained investment remeasured to fair value.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 10 / CAS 33: IFRS 10 uses a SINGLE control model (including 'de facto' control with <50% voting rights and consideration of substantive potential voting rights); ASC 810 uses a DUAL VIE/VOE model and generally ignores de facto control and potential voting rights under the VOE model.

articles.heading: Exit Price, 3-Level Hierarchy & NAV Practical Expedient
articles.text:
• Definition (ASC 820-10-35-2): Exit price in the principal (or most advantageous) market; nonperformance risk incorporated for liabilities.
• Fair Value Hierarchy (ASC 820-10-35-37): Level 1 (quoted prices in active markets), Level 2 (observable inputs), Level 3 (unobservable inputs — requires quantitative range/weighted-average disclosures and rollforward).
• NAV Practical Expedient (ASC 820-10-35-59): Permits measuring qualifying investment fund interests at Net Asset Value (NAV) without leveling them in the hierarchy.
• Contractual Sale Restrictions (ASU 2022-03): Entity-specific contractual restrictions on selling an equity security are NOT considered in measuring its fair value.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Substantially converged with IFRS 13, except US GAAP includes the explicit NAV practical expedient (ASC 820-10-35-59) and allows Day-1 gains/losses when fair value is supported by observable/unobservable exit-price evidence (IFRS 9.B5.1.2A strictly defers Day-1 gains unless based solely on observable market data).

articles.heading: Dual Lessee Model (Finance vs. Operating), Lessor & Sale-Leaseback
articles.text:
• Lessee Dual Model (ASC 842-20-25): BOTH Finance and Operating leases sit on the balance sheet (ROU asset + Lease Liability). However:
  – Finance Lease: Front-loaded expense (ROU amortization + interest expense on lease liability), similar to IFRS 16.
  – Operating Lease: SINGLE STRAIGHT-LINE lease expense in operating income (ROU asset is plugged each period so amortization + interest = straight-line rent); cash payments stay in Operating Cash Flows.
• Scope Exemptions: Short-term lease election (<= 12 months); NO 'low-value asset' exemption (unlike IFRS 16.5(b)).
• Sale-Leaseback (ASC 842-40): If transfer qualifies as a sale under ASC 606, seller-lessee recognizes 100% of the gain/loss immediately (unlike IFRS 16's partial gain restriction).

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • One of the Biggest US GAAP vs. IFRS/CAS Divergences: (1) Lessee P&L — ASC 842 keeps a straight-line Operating Lease expense (preserving EBITDA comparability vs. old GAAP), whereas IFRS 16 / CAS 21 uses a SINGLE front-loaded Finance model for all leases; (2) No low-value asset exemption under ASC 842; (3) Full gain on sale-leaseback under ASC 842 vs. partial gain under IFRS 16.

• Required Disclosures (ASC 850-10-50-1): Nature of relationship(s), description of transactions, dollar amounts for each income statement period, and amounts due from/to related parties at each balance sheet date.
• Arm's-Length Representation (ASC 850-10-50-5): Representations that transactions were on arm's-length terms may NOT be made unless substantiated.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Key Difference from IAS 24 / CAS 36: ASC 850 excludes key management personnel (KMP) compensation disclosures from the financial statement footnotes (covered in SEC proxy statements for public companies), whereas IAS 24.17 mandates KMP compensation disclosures in the footnotes.

articles.text: Distinguishes Recognized (Type 1) vs. Nonrecognized (Type 2) subsequent events occurring after the balance sheet date through the date financial statements are issued (SEC filers) or available to be issued (non-SEC entities).

articles.heading: Type 1 Recognized vs. Type 2 Nonrecognized Events
articles.text:
• Evaluation Cutoff (ASC 855-10-25): SEC filers evaluate subsequent events through the date financial statements are ISSUED; non-SEC entities evaluate through the date financial statements are AVAILABLE TO BE ISSUED (and must disclose that date).
• Recognized vs. Nonrecognized: Conditions existing at the balance sheet date adjust financial statements; conditions arising after the balance sheet date are disclosed if material.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Cutoff Date: ASC 855 runs through the date financial statements are ISSUED (for SEC filers), whereas IAS 10.3 runs through the date financial statements are AUTHORIZED FOR ISSUE (typically slightly earlier).

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes the control-based derecognition criteria for transfers of financial assets (securitizations, receivable factoring, repurchase agreements) requiring legal isolation, transferee pledge/exchange rights, and absence of effective control.

articles.heading: Control-Based Derecognition (Legal Isolation) & Repos
articles.text:
• Three Sale Criteria (ASC 860-10-40-5): (a) Legal isolation — transferred assets are put presumptively beyond the reach of the transferor even in bankruptcy ('true sale' legal opinion); (b) Transferee right to pledge/exchange; (c) Transferor does not maintain effective control (e.g., repurchase agreement).
• No Continuing Involvement Partial Derecognition: Binary sale vs. secured borrowing outcome for entire financial assets (or qualifying 'participating interests').

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 9.3.2 / CAS 23: IFRS 9 focuses primarily on transfer of RISKS AND REWARDS before evaluating control (and permits continuing-involvement partial derecognition); ASC 860 focuses strictly on LEGAL ISOLATION AND CONTROL.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Governs accounting for short-duration and long-duration insurance contracts, modernized by ASU 2018-12 (Long-Duration Targeted Improvements — LDTI) requiring annual assumption updates, market risk benefits at fair value, and upper-medium-grade bond discounting.

articles.heading: Short- vs. Long-Duration Insurance & LDTI Modernization
articles.text: • Long-Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI, ASU 2018-12): Liability for future policy benefits updated annually for cash flow assumptions; discount rate updated quarterly via OCI using upper-medium-grade fixed-income instrument yields; Market Risk Benefits (MRBs) measured at fair value; DAC amortized on a constant-level basis.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Major Divergence from IFRS 17 / CAS 25: IFRS 17 builds a unified current-value Contractual Service Margin (CSM) model across all insurance contracts; US GAAP (ASC 944 + LDTI) retains separate short-duration vs. long-duration models without a CSM.

articles.heading: Scope & Core Objective (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes capitalization of costs incurred to develop computer software to be sold, leased, or otherwise marketed (ASC 985-20) once 'technological feasibility' is established through general release.

articles.heading: Technological Feasibility Window & Amortization
articles.text:
• Capitalization Window (ASC 985-20-25): Expense all costs as R&D (ASC 730) until 'technological feasibility' (detailed program design or working model) is established; capitalize coding/testing costs until product is available for general release to customers.
• Amortization & NRV Test (ASC 985-20-35): Amortize at the greater of revenue-ratio method or straight-line; evaluate unamortized cost against Net Realizable Value each balance sheet date.

articles.heading: Key Cross-Framework Differences
articles.text: • Under US GAAP, software development has two distinct models (ASC 985-20 for external sale vs. ASC 350-40 for internal-use/SaaS); under IFRS, both sit under IAS 38's unified 6-criteria development model.

articles.heading: Top US GAAP vs. IFRS Divergence Map (Reference Only)
articles.text:
• High-Impact Divergence Areas Covered:
  – Revenue (ASC 606 vs. IFRS 15): collectibility threshold, shipping/handling election, IP licensing.
  – Leases (ASC 842 vs. IFRS 16): dual lessee P&L model vs. single front-loaded model; sale-leaseback gain.
  – Financial Instruments & Credit Losses (ASC 320/321/326 vs. IFRS 9): Day-1 lifetime CECL vs. 3-stage ECL; no equity FVOCI.
  – Non-Financial Assets (ASC 330/350/360/730 vs. IAS 2/16/36/38): LIFO, no impairment reversals, R&D expensing, 2-step undiscounted PP&E impairment.
  – Consolidation & Liabilities/Equity (ASC 810/480/470 vs. IFRS 10/IAS 32): VIE/VOE model, mezzanine equity, single-liability convertible debt.
